Cc: Platform Ops <infrastructure@quickcure.health>

Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spike on Hosted API (production)

Hi Priyom,

We're seeing a sharp regression in P95 and P99 response times from the Hosted API starting ~08:45 PST this morning. P95 went from ~420ms to 1.3s and P99 is spiking above 4s for our standard chat calls; error rate (5xx) also climbed from 0.05% to ~0.6%. This is impacting several customer-facing flows.

I've attached two sample request traces and a screenshot of our Grafana dashboard. Trace IDs: qc-req-20261211-1a2b, qc-req-20261211-3c4d. Can we get an urgent triage call? Our SREs are ready to join.

Thanks,
—Alice

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: (none)
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:34:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p95/p99 spike on Hosted API (production) — initial triage

Quick triage notes from the runtime team (observed while looking at the traces Priyom forwarded):

- Root symptom: request pileup in the continuous-batching queue. The batching window has widened due to a short-term shift in request inter-arrival distribution (more concurrent small requests and more long-sequence calls mixed).
- Observed metrics: queue depth peaked ~1200 reqs across the pool; average batch size ~24; mean token processing time unchanged but per-batch overhead is higher when batches are large -> head-of-line effect raises P95/P99.
- Autoscaler behavior: cooldown + provisioning delay (~60–90s) meant new nodes came online after the worst of the backlog; also we're hitting a soft allocation cap in the hosted pool for this tenant mix which slowed scale.

Immediate mitigation options (we can apply these inline):
1) Reduce max_batch_size from 32 -> 8 for the shared Hosted pool to shorten batching latency.
2) Temporarily lower batching_window_ms to 40ms for high-concurrency routes.
3) Create a short-lived reserved fast-lane (2x GPU instances) and route QuickCure traffic there while we stabilize.
4) Enable prefix/KV cache for repeated multi-turn prompts in QuickCure traces to reduce token ops.

I'll coordinate with Dylan to apply (1) and (2) immediately. (3) requires approval from infra lead or exec for extra capacity allocation.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: (none)
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p95/p99 spike on Hosted API (production) — mitigation applied

Applying quick fixes now: reduced max_batch_size -> 8 and batching_window_ms -> 40ms for the affected host pools. Also temporarily bumped the hosted pool +2 instances (standby nodes) to drain the backlog.

Early observations (09:55 PST): P95 dropped from ~1.3s -> ~620ms for QuickCure traffic, error rate trending down. P99 still elevated (~2.6–3.5s) for a subset of long-sequence requests.

I've attached a short logs snapshot (hosted_pool_scale_events.log) to the incident docket. I will keep the scaling in place for 30 minutes and monitor.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: hosted_pool_scale_events.log

Thanks — we can see the P95 improvement on our side, appreciate the quick action. P99 tail remains for conversations with long histories (6+ turns) — those traces show heavy KV cache misses and long decode tails. We have attached two more trace IDs: qc-req-20261211-9e8f, qc-req-20261211-a7b2.

Quick ask: given the impact to product flows, can Redwood provide a one-time credit and a short SLA amendment to cover today's incident window? We're also open to evaluating a Dedicated pool if that's the recommended long-term fix.

—Alice

- 09:13: customer opened ticket with traces
- 09:34: runtime triage (Marissa) -> suggested batch reductions + fast-lane
- 09:47: SRE (Dylan) applied throttles and +2 instances; P95 improved but P99 remains elevated

Attachments: monitoring screenshot and request samples (attached to original thread).

Priyom
